title: Six-leg closed traverse: latitudes, departures and compass-rule adjustment (NAVEDTRA 14070, Figs 7-12 to 7-14; case C3)

source.citation: US Navy, Engineering Aid, NAVEDTRA 14070, chapter 7, Figs 7-12 to 7-14

verification: Recomputed outside the repository in 70-digit decimal arithmetic (Python Decimal with a sin/cos series written for the purpose, no packages) on 2026-11-25. Largest difference between the exact values and the book, over all six lists: 0.0092 ft, except the two entries touched by the book's CD departure erratum, which are NOT checked (null): CD departure (book 39.77; 212.00 x sin 10d49m = 39.7854, the book's own table value 0.18767 gives 39.79) and, because the book's corrections and sums inherit that error, CD adjusted departure (book 39.59, exact 39.6018; difference 0.0118). The tolerance of 0.01 ft is the precision the book prints; no widening was needed. The book's Sigma row and misclosure figures (latitude 0.33, departure 2.24, linear misclosure 2.26 ft, ratio 1:1157) are likewise NOT asserted, because they inherit the same erratum. The exact values are: latitude misclosure 0.3214 ft, departure misclosure 2.2642 ft, linear misclosure 2.2869 ft, relative misclosure 0.00087456 (1 : 1143). They are covered by the exact adjustment test in src/calcs/surveying.rs (the compass rule applied to the book's own printed latitudes and departures matches the book to 0.00515 ft) and by the closed-form and property tests in tests/traverse.rs. The erratum is recorded in planning/REFERENCE_CASES.md (source issues).
